chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and Ya'qub ibn Yazid and Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sahban, altogether, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said:

A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he came out to him in a cloak dyed reddish. So the Bedouin said: O Muhammad! You have come out to me as though you are a young man! So he said: Yes, O Bedouin. I am a young man, son of a young man, brother of a young man. So the Bedouin said: O Muhammad! As for being a young man, then yes; but how are you the son of a young man and brother of a young man? So he said: Have you not heard Allah — Mighty and Majestic — saying: 'They said: We heard a young man mentioning them, called Ibrahim'? So I am the son of Ibrahim. And as for the brother of a young man: a caller called from the sky on the day of Uhud: 'There is no sword except Dhul-Fiqar, and there is no young man except Ali.' So Ali is my brother, and I am his brother.

key_terms.ذو الفقار: Dhul-Fiqar — the legendary sword of Imam Ali, given to him by the Prophet
key_terms.فتى: Young man (fata) — a term connoting bravery, nobility, and spiritual excellence in Arabic (futuwwa)
key_terms.لا سيف إلا ذو الفقار ولا فتى إلا علي: There is no sword except Dhul-Fiqar and no young man except Ali — a heavenly proclamation at the Battle of Uhud

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the famous saying 'There is no sword except Dhul-Fiqar and no young man except Ali'?
ai.summary: A Bedouin compliments the Prophet's youthful appearance, prompting a profound declaration of identity. The Prophet claims the triple title of 'young man' (fata): he is himself a young man; he is the son of Ibrahim, whom the Quran (21:60) calls a 'young man' for his courageous stand against idol-worship; and he is the brother of Ali, who was proclaimed the only true 'young man' by an angelic voice at the Battle of Uhud (3 AH). The famous phrase 'la sayfa illa Dhul-Fiqar, wa la fata illa Ali' ('There is no sword except Dhul-Fiqar, and there is no young man except Ali') became one of the most celebrated declarations in Islamic tradition, linking Ali's martial valor with spiritual nobility.
